text:
alex: Heads-up — autoscaler started removing west-prod-gpu-spot nodepool during the 11:30 surge. Pods with long init (driver + nvlink warmup) were soft-evicted then rescheduled onto on-demand, spiking tail latency. Anyone else seeing this?

maya: Yup, saw the same. PodEviction events + CA logs show bulk delete of empty nodes right after scale-up.

sasha: Logs: CA marked nodes as unneeded because immediate request pressure dropped, but there were a few pending GPU jobs that take ~6-8min to become 'Ready'. CA doesn’t know to wait for driver warmup.

alex: Exactly — warmup + network egress quota checks make those pods appear "not ready" for a while. We should avoid aggressive bulk deletions for GPU pools.

todd: Quick tactical wins: increase scale-down grace, disable empty bulk delete for gpu pools, and prefer binpack expander for GPU-critical workloads. Proposed flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=20m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m, --max-empty-bulk-delete=0, --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45

maya: +1 on the flags. Also recommend enabling --balance-similar-node-groups=true to keep capacity in the same AZ instead of cross-AZ shuffle which worsens network flaps.

sasha: We can also annotate pods we know have long init with ca.redwood-inference/avoid-scale-down: "true" so CA ignores them during unneeded checks. Small change, low risk.

alex: Can you drop the exact CA args we want to test? I want to run a canary in west-prod-eu1.

*todd pasted config snippet*

```
# deployment args for cluster-autoscaler (canary)
--cloud-provider=gce
--expander=binpacking
--scale-down-enabled=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45
--max-empty-bulk-delete=0
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
```

maya: For on-prem/private clusters use-case we should also add a longer --new-pod-scale-up-delay (5m) to avoid thrash when many pods are stuck Pulling images/drivers.

sasha: If we want a smarter long-term solution: tweak the expander to weight nodes by "GPU-warmup-risk" (heuristic: recent driver installs, node age <10m, network egress rate). Not trivial but would reduce these edge cases.

alex: Agreed. For now canary the flags in west-prod-eu1 for 48h. If tail p99 latency improves and we don't lose capacity under steady load, roll to other regions.

infra-bot: rollout start cluster-autoscaler-west-prod-eu1 3187654350

deploy-bot: CA canary applied (args updated). Monitoring: ca.node_changes, pod_evictions, p99-gen-latency.

maya: I'll add a Prometheus alert that watches "ca_bulk_delete > 0 for gpu nodepool" and fires if >1 in 10m window. Also add a dashboard tile for "pending gpu pod init time".

todd: Action items: 1) canary flags (todd) 2) add pod annotation docs + quick helper script (maya) 3) dashboard + alert (sasha) 4) eval expander heuristics (alex+sasha).

alex: Thanks all. Let's check back after 24h and decide whether to expand to apac. :thumbsup:
